question: Do structures detected on 1-minute bars predict the next 1 minute to 1 day by enough to pay costs (A), and does waiting for one improve the entry price of the daily trend trade (B)?

conventions.event: flagged at the close of 1-minute bar t from bars <= t
conventions.fill: open of bar t+1; forward return over h minutes = open[t+1+h] / open[t+1] - 1
conventions.gaps: missing bars and zero-volume runs of >= 5 bars are outages; a forward return whose window touches one is dropped; entry and exit bars must have traded
conventions.inference: sums per calendar day, cluster-robust standard error by day pooled over coins; Bartlett lags across days by horizon {"1": 0, "5": 0, "15": 0, "60": 1, "240": 1, "1440": 3}
conventions.baseline: mean forward return of all bars in the same coin x calendar year x hour of day x volatility state (3 states); family 5 without the hour

selection.basis: DESIGN segment only: 1-minute bars before 2024-01-01, six USDT perpetuals pooled, day-clustered statistics

selected.name: move5_abs2pct_dn
selected.trade: BUY at the next minute's open after the 5-minute return (close to close) falls to -2% or lower (first bar of the crossing; no other such bar in the previous 4); hold 15 minutes
selected.why: Largest day-clustered |t| of any look whose gross size exceeds a taker round trip (design |t| about 10). Same sign in each of the four design years and in each of the six coins; survives a one- and two-minute late entry and a fill at the next minute's volume-weighted price. The pre-stated hypothesis was continuation; the data say reversal, so the trade is the opposite side.

selected.name: move1_z3_dn
selected.trade: BUY at the next minute's open after a 1-minute return below -3 trailing (1-day) standard deviations; hold 15 minutes
selected.why: The most frequent bullish structure with a pooled day-clustered |t| above 7 (about ten events per coin and day), so it is the natural candidate for entry timing in Part B. Known weaknesses on design: gross size (about 8 bp) is below a taker round trip, it is weak in 2022 and on BTC. Expected NOT to pay costs; carried to validation to see whether even the gross effect persists.

selected.name: fund_post5_big
selected.trade: Perpetuals only. At the 00:00 / 08:00 / 16:00 UTC funding stamp, if the last funding rate already paid was >= +3 bp BUY at the stamp's first print (<= -3 bp: SELL); hold 5 minutes
selected.why: A different family (time structure) with a mechanical explanation (positions avoid the payment and return after it). Design |t| about 5, same sign in all four years and all six coins. Gross size (about 8 bp) is below a taker round trip.

validation_plan: Evaluate only the three (definition, horizon) pairs above on 2024-01-01 .. 2025-06-30, once.
Same statistics as on design: events, days, gross bp on the trade side, matched baseline, day-clustered t of the excess, net after a perpetual taker round trip, perpetual maker bound, spot taker.
Pooled over the six perpetuals; by coin and by calendar year as a breakdown; BTC/ETH spot as a cross-check of the two price-based structures.
Execution robustness of the same pairs only: entry one and two minutes late, fills at the minute's volume-weighted price, buy at the next bar's high.
Part B uses the event flags of the selected structures and of their mirrors (part_b_mirror_names) to time entries and exits; no forward-return statistic of the mirrors is computed on validation.

A structure counts as confirmed if the validation estimate has the design sign with day-clustered |t| > 2 (one-sided test of three pre-registered pairs) and as paying costs only if gross minus the taker round trip is positive with the same margin.

verdict_scope: One rare structure only (buying a fall of >= 2% within 5 minutes and holding 15 minutes). Every frequent structure fails to pay costs, and waiting for a structure does not improve the entry price of the daily trend trade.

tests_on_synthetic_data.file: test_eventstudy.py (16 tests, synthetic data only, run before any real bar was used)
tests_on_synthetic_data.no_look_ahead: for all 190 definitions and every feature, values up to bar t are identical when later bars are replaced by a different history (with its own gaps, halts and funding prints) or cut off; a deliberately centred window fails the same check
tests_on_synthetic_data.planted_effect: a 20 bp drift over the 15 minutes after a planted volume spike is recovered at 15, 60, 240 and 1440 minutes and pro rata at 1 and 5 minutes, within 4 standard errors; nothing is found without the plant; a move inside the event bar or between its close and the next open is not credited
tests_on_synthetic_data.gaps: every forward return whose window touches a missing bar or a halt (>= 5 zero-volume bars) is dropped

conclusions: 630 definition x horizon looks on design (six USDT perpetuals, 2020-2023) plus 11 descriptive autocorrelation statistics. 187 looks have a day-clustered |t| above 3 (about 1.7 expected by chance); their median size is 3.6 bp against a taker round trip of 12-14 bp. 49 exceed a taker round trip: 47 in the large-move family (30 after falls, 14 pooled over both directions and carried by the falls, 3 after rises) and 2 elsewhere. At the one-day horizon 1 of 88 looks reaches |t| > 3, which is what chance gives: nothing on a 1-minute bar predicts the next day.

Volume and trade-count spikes, wick shape (exhaustion versus continuation), order-flow imbalance, 3-sigma moves, return autocorrelation, hour of day, minute of the hour and funding windows are statistically visible and economically 5 to 100 times too small. Wick shape adds nothing. Extreme taker pressure reverses slightly rather than continues.

At one minute BTC and ETH have no autocorrelation to speak of (reversal trade within 0.01 bp of zero). Where a 1-minute reversal exists when measured from the closing print (XRP: +0.26 bp per trade over the design period; DOGE in 2020 and 2023), most of it disappears when the trade starts at the next open (XRP: +0.04 bp, so 83% is gone): it is bid-ask bounce and cannot be captured. Five-minute returns are negatively autocorrelated in 2021-2023 (-0.03 to -0.06), worth about 0.3 bp per trade.

Selected pair 1 (buy a fall of >= 2% in 5 minutes, hold 15 minutes): design 7965 events, 40.4 bp gross, t 9.9, net of taker costs 26.7 bp; validation 1004 events, 47.1 bp, t 5.0, net 33.4 bp (t 3.6). Confirmed.

Selected pair 2 (buy a 1-minute fall beyond 3 sigma, hold 15 minutes): design 7.9 bp gross (t 7.4), net -5.4 bp; validation 3.7 bp (t 3.2), net -9.6 bp. The gross effect persists at half size and does not pay.

Selected pair 3 (after a funding stamp with |last funding| >= 3 bp, hold 5 minutes): design 8.6 bp (t 5.0); validation 2.2 bp (t 0.9). Not confirmed, and zero under any fill other than the very first print after the stamp.

Part B (entry timing of the daily trend rule, BTC and ETH spot): waiting up to 4 hours for the first 3-sigma dip instead of buying at the 00:00 UTC open gave 18.6 bp on design (t 2.14, 151 entries) and 7.4 bp on validation (t 0.71, 63 entries); the structure adds 0.5 bp over simply waiting until 04:00 (t 0.08). No measurable improvement; exits likewise.

Verdict: edge_after_taker_costs in a narrow sense (one rare crash-time structure, on paper, under the cost convention of the study). Frequent 1-minute structures do not pay costs and do not improve the entry of a daily trade.
caveats: Execution in crash minutes is untested: fills are assumed at the first print of the next minute with 1-2 bp slippage. The validated rebound is intact at the minute's volume-weighted price and one or two minutes late, negative at the worst print of the first minute, and roughly break-even with 30 bp of extra round-trip cost.
Rare and lumpy: on validation 1,004 events on 157 of 547 days over six coins; the 5 best days carry 30% and the 20 best 72% of the total. Events bunch across coins.
Tail risk: single 15-minute losses of 15% to 30% are in the sample (19 May 2021, 12 March 2020). About 4% of design trades lose more than 5%.
Universe: six coins that are large today. An hourly check on all liquid USDT perpetuals (design only) shows about one third of the rebound and none for perpetuals that were later delisted.
Design-only observation, not validated: the first 2% fall of a cascade rebounds by only about 12 bp; the average is carried by later legs and by the largest falls.
Maker figures are upper bounds: a resting order fills when the price trades through it and the signals that run away unfilled are the best ones (shown with a fill simulation on design).
Halts are excluded after the fact: an event followed by an exchange outage is dropped, which a live trader cannot do.
Funding is not charged (irrelevant for the 5- and 15-minute pairs). Standard errors are slightly liberal at the one-day horizon; nothing is claimed there.
Part B has little power on rule-change days alone (214 entries, sd about 100 bp); the all-days version (about 4,000 observations) resolves about 5 bp and still shows nothing.

Protocol: the execution check of the funding pair was run after the selection was written and before validation was loaded; it already showed the first-print problem on design. An initial scan of bar timestamps and zero-volume counts covered the validation period; no price or return of that period was examined before the validation run.
Only 1-minute bars were available: no order book, no trades inside the minute, no other exchanges.

plain_language.method: Six USDT perpetuals (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE) on 1-minute bars; BTC/ETH spot and PAXG spot as cross-checks. Design = bars before 2024-01-01, validation = 2024-01-01 to 2025-06-30, hold-out never loaded. An event is flagged at the close of bar t from bars up to t and filled at the open of bar t+1; forward returns run from that open over 1, 5, 15, 60, 240 and 1440 minutes. Missing bars, and halts printed as runs of five or more zero-volume bars, are gaps: any forward return whose window touches one is dropped. Statistics are sums per calendar day, clustered by day across coins, and measured against the mean forward return of bars in the same coin, year, hour of day and volatility state. Round-trip costs: perpetual taker 12 bp (BTC, ETH) or 14 bp, maker bound 4 bp, spot taker 22 or 24 bp.
plain_language.family_1_volume_and_trade_spikes: Bars with quote volume or trade count above 5x or 10x the median of the previous 60 bars. After a down bar on a spike the price recovers a little (1.6 bp over 5 minutes at 5x volume, 4.5 bp at 10x trade count); after an up bar it continues by a similar amount (0.8 and 4.5 bp). Wick shape adds nothing: a down bar that closes at its low and one with a long lower wick are followed by the same recovery (1.4 and 1.7 bp at 5 minutes). The largest effects are bars closing at their extreme on a 10x trade-count spike: 7 bp at 5 minutes and 13 bp at an hour after up bars, below a taker round trip, and the up side lives in 2021 and in XRP and DOGE (2022: 0.9 bp, BTC: -0.7 bp at 5 minutes). Two of 216 looks exceed a taker round trip with |t| > 3 (at 4 hours and one day, |t| 3.1 and 3.6), which is not evidence with this many looks.
plain_language.family_2_order_flow_imbalance: Taker-buy share of quote volume over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes, as a z-score against its own trailing day. Extreme buying or selling is followed by a small move the other way: 0.4 to 1.2 bp over 5 to 15 minutes at |z| > 2 (|t| up to 10.8), 1.5 bp at an hour. The 1-minute extreme at |z| > 3 (3199 events) shows nothing. Pressure does not continue, and the reversal is an order of magnitude below costs.
plain_language.family_3_large_moves: Returns over 1, 5 and 15 minutes beyond 3, 5 and 8 trailing standard deviations, and 5-minute moves of 2% or more. After falls the price rebounds: 7.9 bp over 15 minutes after a 3-sigma minute, 19.5 bp after 5 sigma, 44.2 bp after 8 sigma, 40.4 bp after a 2% fall in 5 minutes (92 bp at one hour), with the same sign in every design year and every coin. After rises it tends to continue (4.6, 12.0, 20.4 bp), but only in 2021 and in XRP and DOGE: zero in 2022 and on BTC. These are the only looks whose size exceeds a taker round trip. At one day nothing is significant.
plain_language.family_4_autocorrelation_and_bid_ask_bou: Trading the sign of the trailing return on every bar: +0.06 bp of continuation at one minute (t 5.5), then 0.13 to 0.31 bp of reversal at 5 minutes (|t| 8.2 to 11.3); nothing from a 60-minute return and nothing at one day. BTC and ETH have no 1-minute autocorrelation to speak of. Where a 1-minute reversal exists when measured from the closing print (XRP: +0.26 bp per trade; DOGE in 2020 and 2023), most of it disappears when the trade starts at the next open (XRP: +0.04 bp): that part is bid-ask bounce. The step from a close to the next open, about one tick, is 0.1 bp on BTC and about 1 bp on XRP, DOGE and SOL. Five-minute returns are negatively autocorrelated in 2021-2023 (-0.03 to -0.06).
plain_language.family_5_time_structure: No hour of the day reaches |t| = 3 (largest 2.2 of 24). The first minute of each quarter hour (:00, :15, :30, :45) returns +0.57 to +0.75 bp (t about 6.7 each, on every coin and on spot), partly given back in the next two minutes; it was 1.3-1.8 bp in 2021 and 0.1-0.2 bp in 2023. Around funding stamps there is nothing unconditional; when the last paid funding was at least 3 bp the price moves 8.6 bp with the payers in the 5 minutes after the stamp (t 5.0), which the execution check shows to be complete within the first prints after the stamp.
plain_language.cross_checks_spot_and_gold: The same grid on BTC and ETH spot agrees with the perpetuals of the same coins (correlation of excess returns over 612 looks: 0.96). On PAXG spot about a quarter of the minutes have no trade and every short horizon shows reversal of 1 to 5 bp, which is what prints alternating between the two sides of a wide spread look like, against a 24 bp round trip; a 2% fall in 5 minutes occurred 6 times in the design period. There is nothing to trade on 1-minute gold-token bars.
plain_language.execution_checks: Rebound after a 2% fall (design, 15 minutes): 40.4 bp at the next open, 34.5 bp one minute late, 29.8 bp two minutes late, 37.0 bp at the minute's volume-weighted price, -37.8 bp at the worst print of the first minute. Post-funding move (design, 5 minutes): 8.6 bp at the first print, -0.6 bp one minute late, 0.3 bp at the minute's volume-weighted price: a first-print artefact. Resting orders (design): a bid at the first print of the next minute, alive for one minute, fills 93% of the 3-sigma dips; the filled ones earn 7.0 bp, the ones that ran away unfilled would have earned 19.4 bp, and the net per signal with a maker entry and a taker exit is -1.5 bp, not the +3.9 bp of the flat maker bound.
plain_language.selection: Three (definition, horizon) pairs were chosen on design evidence and written to SELECTION.json before any validation bar was loaded: buy after a fall of at least 2% in 5 minutes and hold 15 minutes (largest day-clustered |t| among the looks that exceed a taker round trip; the pre-stated hypothesis was continuation and the data said rebound); buy after a 1-minute fall beyond 3 sigma and hold 15 minutes (the most frequent bullish structure with |t| > 7, selected with its weaknesses stated: below costs, weak in 2022 and on BTC); trade with the payers at the first print after a funding stamp when the last paid funding was at least 3 bp and hold 5 minutes (a different family with a mechanical explanation). Confirmation rule, written with the selection: same sign with day-clustered |t| > 2; pays costs only if gross minus the taker round trip is positive with the same margin. The execution check of the funding pair was run after the selection and before validation; the selection was left as written.
plain_language.validation: Pair 1: 1004 events on 157 days, 47.1 bp gross (design 40.4), day-clustered t 5.0, hit rate 64%, net of taker costs 33.4 bp (t 3.6); positive in 2024 and 2025 and in each coin; 40.0 bp one minute late, 43.9 bp at the minute's volume-weighted price, -24.2 bp at the worst print; 30% of the total from the 5 best days and 72% from the 20 best. Confirmed. Pair 2: 3.7 bp gross (design 7.9), t 3.2, net -9.6 bp, maker bound -0.3 bp: the gross effect persists at half size and does not pay. Pair 3: 2.2 bp (design 8.6), t 0.9: not confirmed.
plain_language.part_b_entry_timing: Days on which the 50/100/200-day rule raises a coin's weight: 151 on design, 63 on validation (BTC and ETH spot). Waiting up to 4 hours for the first 1-minute fall beyond 3 sigma instead of buying at the 00:00 UTC open: design mean 18.6 bp, median 30.8, t 2.14, worse price in 28% of cases; validation mean 7.4 bp, median 14.1, t 0.71, worse in 37%. Simply buying at 04:00 gave 16.5 and 10.9 bp, so the structure adds 2.2 bp (t 0.24) and -3.6 bp (t -0.67). Up to 24 hours: 11.5 bp (t 1.00) and -4.4 bp (t -0.25). On every day of both segments (3994 observations) the 4-hour wait gives 3.0 bp (t 1.31). The 2% fall almost never occurs inside the window (0% within 4 hours, 7% within 24), so that trader ends up buying at the end of the window (-39.5 bp, t -1.77 for 24 hours). Exits, selling at the first 1-minute rise beyond 3 sigma within 4 hours: 4.7 bp (t 0.50, 208 exits). No measurable improvement. For a price close to a random walk no waiting rule changes the expected fill; the most a structure can add is its own forward return, a few basis points here, against about 100 bp of noise from a 4-hour wait.
plain_language.validated_structure_closer_look_design_o: Not validated; looked at after the validation run, on design data. First 2% fall of a cascade (none on that coin in the previous hour): 11.7 bp (median 33.4); later legs: 61.5 bp; one position at a time per coin: 27.1 bp. By size of the fall: 23 bp for falls of 2.0-2.5%, 76 bp for 3-5%, 190 bp beyond 5%. Single trades net of costs: standard deviation 329 bp, worst -2949 bp. Extra round-trip cost that the pair can bear: per event 6.7 bp remain on design and 13.4 bp on validation with +20 bp, -3.3 and 3.4 bp with +30 bp. Hourly check on all liquid USDT perpetuals including delisted ones (buy at the next hourly open after an hourly fall of 5%, hold one hour): 33 bp (t 1.4) on 248 perpetuals, 93 bp (t 3.2) on the six coins of this study, -15 bp on perpetuals that were later delisted: the rebound belongs to large liquid coins.
plain_language.what_it_means_for_the_idea: As a source of trades, ordinary 1-minute structures do not work for an account that pays taker fees: the structure is there, and it is worth tenths of a basis point to a few basis points per trade. As an entry timer for a daily trade they do not work either: entering at the daily open is as good as anything tested. The one thing that pays on paper is liquidity provision in a crash (buying a fall of 2% within 5 minutes): rare, fat-tailed and decided by execution in the worst minute of the day. It deserves its own study with order-book or trade data, a position cap and the locked hold-out before any money is put on it.
